The purpose of the satirical film Don’t Look Up is primarily to make a commentary on the American response to the issue of climate change. The comet is portrayed as a big event that is going to inevitably hit the Earth and extinct humanity. Climate change is a large issue that was discovered many years ago and threatens to largely hurt humanity, and already is killing many species and damaging ecosystems. The film parodies scientists, deniers, profiteers, and celebrities on…

Don’t Look Up is a really entertaining watch mostly because of how well it uses satire to reflect real world reactions to crisis and media obsession. The cast is huge and it works surprisingly well, with Jennifer Lawrence delivering another strong performance, while Meryl Streep and Jonah Hill lean fully into their absurd, exaggerated roles in a way that fits the tone. Leonardo DiCaprio also stands out in a role that feels a bit different from what he usually does,…

Don't Look Up is as delightful as it is horrifying. An on-the-nose commentary about our societal priorities, this movie is a paradoxically entertaining reminder about the dangers of distraction in the face of global catastrophe. Featuring an amazingly talented star-studded cast, Don't Look Up combines the outrageous humor of Idiocracy, the down-to-Earth insight of The Big Short, and the feeling of unavoidable finality felt in Knowing. Overall, a classic whose message will last about as long as our ozone layer.
